rf1974.title: Regeringsform (1974:152)
rf1974.note: Ch. 1 § 1 (popular sovereignty, representative democracy, and municipal self-government); ch. 3 § 1 (direct, free, secret, proportional Riksdag elections), § 2 (one chamber of 349 members), § 3 (ordinary elections every four years); ch. 8 § 2 (law on advisory national referendums, constitutional referendums, and European Parliament elections); ch. 14 § 1 (municipal decisions are taken by elected assemblies).

vallag2005.title: Vallag (2005:837)
vallag2005.note: Ch. 1 § 2-3: elections are always held on a Sunday; ordinary Riksdag, regional, and municipal elections are held on the same day, the second Sunday of September; European Parliament elections in June every five years unless the Council of the EU sets April, May, or July. The act also governs re-runs (omval) and extra elections, and Sametinget elections by reference from the Sametingslag.

kommunallag2017.title: Kommunallag (2017:725)
kommunallag2017.note: Ch. 5 § 1: the council (fullmäktige) decides on referendums in the municipality or region and on extra elections; ch. 8: consultative referendums and the popular initiative of ten percent of the electorate. Municipal executive committees and their chairs are chosen by the council.

folkomrostningslag1994.title: Lag (1994:692) om kommunala folkomröstningar
folkomrostningslag1994.note: Procedure for municipal and regional referendums under the Local Government Act: the council sets the day, the question, and the options; the municipal election committee runs the vote.

sametingslag1992.title: Sametingslag (1992:1433)
sametingslag1992.note: Ch. 2 § 2: Sametinget has 31 members chosen by election; ch. 3 § 1: elections every four years on the third Sunday of May; ch. 3 § 2: the country is one constituency, and the election is run by Sametinget's election board, the central election authority, and the county administrative board.

kyrkolag1998.title: Lag (1998:1591) om Svenska kyrkan
kyrkolag1998.note: From 1 January 2000 the Church of Sweden is a religious community separate from the state, organized in parishes and dioceses with the Church Assembly (kyrkomötet) as its highest decision-making body; its elections follow its own church order.

val_allmanna.title: Allmänna val i Sverige
val_allmanna.note: Four general elections: the Riksdag, regional councils, municipal councils, and the European Parliament; ordinary elections to the first three on the second Sunday of September every four years.

val_valkretsar.title: Valkretsar och valdistrikt
val_valkretsar.note: Sweden is divided into 29 constituencies for Riksdag elections; 310 of the 349 seats are fixed constituency seats and 39 are adjustment seats. Regions and municipalities may divide themselves into constituencies; 90 percent of their seats are fixed. Sweden is one constituency for the European Parliament, with 21 of 720 seats. Each municipality is divided into election districts of about 1,000-2,000 voters.

val_rrk_tidigare.title: Tidigare valresultat i val till riksdag, region och kommun
val_rrk_tidigare.note: Summaries and links to the full result presentations on historik.val.se for 2002-2018, and the re-runs in Orsa (2003), Västra Götaland and Örebro (2011), Båstad (2015), and Falun (2019).

val_folkomrostningar.title: Folkomröstningar
val_folkomrostningar.note: Sweden has held six national referendums, all advisory. Municipal and regional referendums are always advisory, decided by the council or forced by an initiative of ten percent of the electorate, and run and reported by the municipality or region. Links the lists of held national and municipal referendums.

val_nationella_lista.title: Lista genomförda nationella folkomröstningar
val_nationella_lista.note: Six rows (source: the Government), list updated 2021-08-18: 1922 Rusdrycksförbud, 1955 Högertrafik, 1957 Tjänstepension, 1980 Kärnkraftsfrågan, 1994 EU-medlemskap, 2003 Införande av euron.

val_kommunala_lista.title: Lista över genomförda kommunala folkomröstningar
val_kommunala_lista.note: List updated 2026-11-10, from 1980: 169 municipal referendums (one regional, Västerbottens landsting in 2013), with year, municipality, question, and whether held with a general election.

val_sameting_tidigare.note: Results of every Sametinget election from 2005 to 2021, with links to the full presentations on historik.val.se.

val_sameting_2025.title: Valresultat i sametingsvalet 2025
val_sameting_2025.note: Result of the re-run of 5 October 2025; the decision on the result of the ordinary election of 18 May 2025 was set aside and never became final.

val_omval.title: Omval och extra val
val_omval.note: The Election Review Board (Valprövningsnämnden) may order a re-run (omval), held within three months; between ordinary elections the Government may call an extra Riksdag election and a regional or municipal council an extra council election.

scb_lan_kommuner.note: SCB keeps the official register of regional divisions and their codes: "Sverige har idag 21 län och 290 kommuner."

classes.finest_note: Valmyndigheten publishes final counts by election district (valdistrikt) from 2002; SCB's database has every election from 1973 by municipality and constituency, and SCB's printed volumes for 1970-1998 go down to election district.
classes.note: One chamber since 1971: 350 members elected in 1970 and 1973, 349 from 1976. Party-list proportional representation in 29 constituencies (fixed constituency seats) with national adjustment seats; modified Sainte-Laguë with a first divisor of 1.2 since 2018 (1.4 before), 4 percent national threshold or 12 percent in a constituency. Terms of three years until 1994 and four years since. Extra elections are possible on the Government's decision but none has been held under the 1974 Instrument of Government.

cadence.vacancy_rule: Vallag ch. 14: a vacancy is filled by a new count (ny sammanräkning) from the same party's list; there are no by-elections.

classes.note: Directly elected lower house of the bicameral Riksdag under the Riksdag Act of 1866. Mostly single-member constituencies with plurality voting until 1908; party-list proportional representation from 1911, universal suffrage for men in 1909 and for women in 1921. Ordinary elections every three years until 1920 and every four years from 1924, with extra elections in spring 1887, spring 1914, 1921, and 1958.

classes.name: Kyrkoval i Svenska kyrkan
classes.name_en: Church of Sweden elections (Church Assembly, diocesan, and church councils)
classes.note: Members of the Church of Sweden aged 16 and over elect the Church Assembly (kyrkomötet), the 13 diocesan assemblies (stiftsfullmäktige), and the church councils of the 571 pastorates and independent parishes (kyrkofullmäktige) on the same day every four years: 2001, 2005, 2009, 2013, 2017, 2021, and 2025 (third Sunday of September), next in September 2029. About 850,000 valid votes were cast for church councils in 2025. Before 2000, church elections were held under state law while the Church of Sweden was the state church.
classes.disposition_reason: Since 2000 the Church of Sweden is a religious community separate from the state; its elections are held under its own church order and run and published by the church, not by a public election authority.

access.evidence: Church Assembly and diocesan results by parish for 2013-2025 and church council results by electoral area and parish for 2025, as Excel files.

classes.name: Statschef (kungen)
classes.disposition_reason: The head of state is the hereditary monarch under the Act of Succession; there is no election.
classes.note: Sweden has no directly elected executive at any tier.

classes.name: Statsministeromröstning i riksdagen
classes.name_en: Prime minister vote in the Riksdag
classes.disposition_reason: The Speaker proposes a prime minister and the Riksdag votes (Instrument of Government ch. 6); the proposal fails only if more than half the members vote against. This is a members' vote recorded in the Riksdag's minutes, not a public election.

classes.name: Val av kommunstyrelse och regionstyrelse
classes.name_en: Municipal and regional executive committees and their chairs
classes.disposition_reason: Executive committees, their chairs, and the boards of each municipality and region are chosen by the council (Local Government Act ch. 5-6); these are councillors' votes, not public elections.

classes.name: Val av nämndemän
classes.disposition_reason: Lay judges for the district, administrative, and appeal courts are elected by municipal and regional councils; judges are appointed by the Government. No judicial office is filled by a public election.

classes.name: Partiernas provval
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose and order their candidates under their own rules, sometimes by member ballots (provval); no state authority runs or records them.
